newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy 1996 machine tool output seen up slightly.
newsitem.headline: Italy 1996 machine tool output seen up slightly.

text.p: Italian machine tool production in 1996 is seen rising 8.4 percent after a boom year in 1995 which saw a 40.7 percent surge, the producers' body UCIMU said.
Exports this year were seen up 14.8 percent with a sector trade surplus up 11.3 percent at 1.17 trillion lire, while domestic demand was 7.8 percent up at 5.14 trillion lire.

On the international level, the sector had seen an easing of the rate of development "due to a slowdown in the expansive cycle and less dynamism in our investments," UCIMU director general Alfredo Mariotti told a news conference.

Order books, currently standing at around six months, had allowed companies to maintain 1995 output rates with positive effects on job levels with employment in the sector up about 4.0 percent in the first nine months of this year.
Exports to France, Spain, Brazil and Russia were continuing to increase but levels were more limited in Germany and the United States due to the effects of a stronger lira.
For 1997, UCIMU saw positive prospects in Italy's main foreign markets.
Imports, which rose to 57.2 percent in 1995, were seen posting an increase of just 16.6 percent this year.
